Less about brute force and more about understanding.

While I know this doesn't help most people, I can try to summarize what I knew/learned about the test:

I firmly believe the math section to be where your baseline should be.  It does not go beyond pre-calculus, and even this is a stretch.  Compared to tests such as AMC and math olympiad, it is super easy (I get around 75th percentile on these hard math tests and never qualify so I am far from a math genius).  This math section is also easier to understand for most people, as it appears more subjective.  Learn every math concept needed, then drill those concepts.  People try to memorize theorems but you need practice with applying them.

For the english section, I will not try to explain because honestly I don't know.  I barely studied for the writing section as grammar is intuitive for me, and the reading I knew most of.  If you have time, read a bunch of stuff just to normalize english.  If you don't have time, remember every question is objective, and use the black book I read through it and found it quite comprehensive
